A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conditional-testing framework and KRR confidence bounds. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of error rates, local sensitivity, output-kernel choices, bootstrap calibration, and dynamical-system monitoring in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds comparisons of bootstrap methods and regularization sensitivity, particularly in Appendix B and Figure 6.

M1.justification: v2 adds a distinct wild-bootstrap calibration procedure using residual perturbations, centered Gaussian multipliers, and studentization by the theoretical uncertainty term (Appendix B, Algorithm 3). This substantially extends threshold computation by avoiding repeated KRR refitting. The original resampling procedure, test statistic, and KRR estimator remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic conditional regression, discrepancies in rarely sampled regions, comparisons of moments and distributions, and switched linear-system monitoring. The added bootstrap experiments vary methods and settings within these retained tasks and data-generating scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds the evaluated bootstrap comparator of Singh and Vijaykumar alongside the authors' naive and wild variants. Hu and Lei remains the comparator in Figure 2 with the same described oracle information.

E3.justification: v2 adds a regularization sweep over 0.001, 0.1, and 1, and drops n=250 from the sample-size sweep. For Figure 2's right panel, v1 Appendix F.2.1 specifies 100 samples, whereas v2 Table 4 reports 500; this establishes a reported-setting revision, not necessarily a rerun. The new Figure 6b setting is inconsistent: Appendix B says n=500, while G.2.5 says n=50.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends the existing bootstrap sensitivity study with regularization sensitivity and comparisons of alternative calibration and studentization procedures. The output-kernel analysis, analytical-versus-bootstrap comparison, and monitoring case study remain; moving monitoring into Section 5 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 6 displays 2.5% and 97.5% quantile bands; v2 explicitly omits uncertainty intervals from its expanded Figure 6 for readability. The reported 100 experiment runs and the general repeated-sampling and quantile-reporting practice remain.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds error-rate curves for the wild-bootstrap variants and regularization-dependent results, including type-I error inflation under weak regularization. The n=250 results disappear from Figure 6, and the sigma=0.01 series disappears from Figure 7. The principal findings in the retained regression, kernel-comparison, and monitoring examples remain.

T1.justification: v2 introduces explicit functional-representation conditions in Assumption 4.5 and establishes the kernel-feature representation result in Proposition A.1. It also replaces pairwise independence with independence of the transition-pair process and corrects a missing squared norm in the proof of Corollary E.20. The main confidence inequalities and most proofs are retained from v1.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the headline contribution by distinguishing the basic expectation test from functional tests and full-distribution two-sample tests obtained through suitable embeddings. v1 called the basic construction a conditional two-sample test. Moment and distribution testing were already present in v1 Appendix A; the finite-sample and non-i.i.d. novelty claims remain.

C2.justification: Remark G.1 newly acknowledges that nonlinear output kernels need not preserve the RKHS-membership assumption, qualifying v1's description of the simulations as well-specified. v2 also discusses regularization-dependent calibration failures and the absence of a general theoretical analysis for its extended wild bootstrap. It adds a frequentist-versus-Bayesian interpretation of the confidence bounds.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit Gram-matrix implementation steps for the wild bootstrap and calibration complexity estimates in Table 1. It abbreviates existing algorithm interfaces, including removing the explicit alpha/2 argument from Algorithm 1, although Appendix B retains the error allocation. The code-access link and hardware remain; many expanded table entries relocate previously stated settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Singh and Vijaykumar's KRR inference work, additional GP references, and Li et al.'s 2024 vector-valued learning-rate work. Appendix D expands the distinction between learning rates and uniform confidence bounds. Several earlier embedding and Bayesian-inference references are removed, while the principal conditional-testing positioning remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its abstract and contribution narrative are rewritten around functional testing, and Appendix A is substantially restructured. Functional testing gains Section 4.3, algorithms receive a separate appendix, monitoring moves into the main results, and experimental documentation is reorganized into more specific subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a narrower publication layout without v1's running headers and extensively rearranges displays. The monitoring figure moves into the main text with side-by-side panels, Figure 6 becomes a two-row comparison, a complexity table is added, and hyperparameter tables are expanded and regrouped. Figure 1's reversed rejection/acceptance colors in the caption are corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly separates expectation testing from distribution testing and corrects the overly broad description of theoretical coverage through Remark G.1. The new bootstrap option and regularization study improve practical assessment by exposing calibration failures. These gains are limited by conflicting sample counts for Figure 6b and the omission of its uncertainty bands, which weaken reproducibility and interpretation.
